item.text: {"question_id":"5B.4","answer":"In 2023, China adopted or operated formal rules addressing competition and market regulation, including supporting anti-monopoly regulations effective in April and a revised Administrative Reconsideration Law enacted in September but scheduled to take effect in January 2024 (BATCH-0012-E007; BATCH-0019-E002). Xi also announced or reaffirmed expanded market access, foreign-investment, business-environment, and intellectual-property commitments, but the passage supplies no independent enforcement test (BATCH-0010-E010). Official indicators showing new market entities, trade, and employment describe economic activity, not fair or predictable rule enforcement (BATCH-0018-E005; BATCH-0018-E006). Contrary evidence is substantial: foreign businesses faced raids and vague counter-espionage rules that created uncertainty, labor rights and labor laws were inconsistently enforced, and a geographically limited study found politically connected firms received higher corporate social-credit scores (BATCH-0010-E028; BATCH-0022-E014; BATCH-0001-E013; BATCH-0008-E005). Early-2023 private fixed-asset investment growth was only 0.4%, versus 9.4% for state-owned and state-holding investment, but this descriptive divergence does not by itself establish discriminatory causation (BATCH-0022-E004). The evidence therefore supports formal rule-building and some economic activity, but not a conclusion that rules were consistently fair, predictable, or equally enforced during the 2023 period.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E007","BATCH-0019-E002","BATCH-0010-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0010-E028","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0001-E013","BATCH-0008-E005","BATCH-0022-E004","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The revised Administrative Reconsideration Law was enacted in 2023 but did not take effect until 2024, so it cannot establish 2023 implementation or outcomes.","The standards evidence concerns a regulation whose legal effect began in 2024, and the supplied passage provides no compliance or competition results.","Official claims and aggregate indicators do not independently test equal treatment, predictability, or enforcement against connected actors.","The social-credit evidence covers Zhejiang only and has uncertain observation-year fit; personal Xi attribution is not demonstrated for that study.","The private-investment divergence is descriptive and does not establish the causes or legal fairness of the difference.","The supplied evidence lacks systematic case-level enforcement data for competition, property, trade, investment, and entrepreneurship rules."],"corrections_made":["Removed the claim that 2023 standards and administrative-reconsideration measures demonstrated 2023 enforcement.","Reclassified market-entity, trade, manufacturing, employment, and administrative-reconsideration counts as contextual outcomes rather than proof of fair enforcement.","Integrated foreign-business uncertainty, labor-law inconsistency, politically connected social-credit advantages, and private-state investment divergence as material contrary or qualifying evidence.","Preserved the distinction between Xi-attributed announcements or central-government action and evidence that does not establish Xi’s personal role or causal responsibility."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if independent 2023 evidence becomes available on actual competition, property, investment, trade, labor, and administrative-review enforcement, including remedies and treatment of politically connected firms.","Reopen if evidence clarifies the observation period and broader geographic coverage of the social-credit study.","Reopen if longitudinal private-investment and firm-entry evidence can distinguish regulatory discrimination from macroeconomic or sectoral conditions."]}
